correctness.rationale: The stated rare-intensity theorem holds. With z=bt, Delta=lambda b^2/a and Q=2 Delta (E exp(zJ/b)-1-z E[J/b])/z^2, algebra gives c/b=sup (1-1/M)/z, where M=(1+Q)/(1+Delta E[(J/b)^2]); for z outside the candidate moment domain the objective is already bounded by 1/z. Laplace integration of the endpoint distribution gives E exp(zJ/b)~K exp(z)z^(-beta), with log derivative tending to 1 by tilted concentration. The trial z=L+(beta+3)log L gives objective (1-o(1))/L. For each fixed epsilon, the bounds Delta exp(z)/3 and 1/z exclude respectively z<=(1-epsilon)L and z>=(1+epsilon)L. This also supplies the missing justification of interior attainment for all sufficiently small intensities: the continuous extension at zero is only O(Delta), and the objective tends to zero at infinity. Thus every maximizing z is asymptotic to L and Q diverges there. Stationarity then gives Q/z->1, recovering the tilt expansion upon taking logs; the inverse objective is z+z/(M-1)=z+1+o(1). A fresh non-integer test with a mixture of an atom at zero and Beta(1,1/2), whose endpoint amplitude is 2/3, produced tilt errors 0.72807, 0.12234, 0.01705 and inverse-scale errors 0.77709, 0.12799, 0.01763 at L=60,600,6000, respectively. Numerical stationarity is corroboration only.
residual_risks: Step 3's initial inference of a positive interior maximum from continuity, positivity and decay alone does not hold at arbitrary intensity. For instance, with uniform scaled jumps and Delta>=12, coefficient comparison gives the sharp scale Delta/[12(1+Delta/3)] attained only in the z->0 limit of the objective. The trial-point argument proves interior attainment in the stated rare-intensity regime, so no change to the theorem is required.
The endpoint has no atom, but atoms elsewhere are allowed; no rate or uniformity in the jump law is certified.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Writing m2=E J^2, its L'=log(V_lambda/(lambda m2))=L+log(b^2/m2)+o(1) and K'=2K b^2/m2. Then (beta+3)log L'=(beta+3)log L+o(1), so L'-log K'=L-log(2K)+o(1). Both expansions coincide, including the constant term.

value.rationale: The mathematical question is substantive: a leading Bernstein scale does not distinguish endpoint behavior, whereas this sharp true-variance asymptotic recovers both the power exponent and amplitude and locates the optimizing tilt. The value is in that theorem, not in another rendering of the same theorem; the duplicate coverage independently prevents acceptance.
